AITA for not helping my girlfriend bring her work computer in the house? | Some background info: I drive nights for a beverage distributor and my runs may be 11 - 14 hours long, she works for a bank in a back stage office (she doesn't keep bank hours, she usually works 7am until 4-5 ish). I have a routine of chores, food, and exercise that works well during the week, so long as my nightly runs don't take too long. If one night goes long, it messes up the rest of the week (I can go in to greater detail, if needed). This was one of those weeks, so I'm running behind.

This week, she was selected as someone who can work from home. She went in to work in the morning, packed up a laptop, a couple monitors, mouse, and keyboard. She's on the clock for this. She returned home a few minutes after I did.

She was expecting me to help her unload her car and help carry stuff to her desk upstairs. She was shocked when I told her no, because I don't work for the bank and I was busy with a couple chores as a part of my routine that I'm running behind on(prepping food for the dogs and cats and cleaning litter boxes).

In the time I took for me to put some cat food in three dishes, and clean out 4 litter boxes, she had everything in her "office". But now she isn't talking to me.

So, AITA and need to apologize?

AITA for making a stink about traveling with our 4 month old for Christmas? | First time SAHM to my 4 month old son. MIL is insisting that we all fly to visit my husband's extended family for their Christmas (the 28th). I am super reluctant to travel, given the germy-ness, expense, inconvenience of lugging stuff, and the fact that my otherwise loveable 4 month old is prone to meltdowns (as 4 month olds often are). I am the primary caregiver, have done 99% of the night shifts, and am the de facto baby wrangler when baby is losing his shit, as he often does because he nearly never naps and totally refuses a pacifier or bottle (we're exclusively breastfeeding). I am exhausted most days and haven't slept for more than 4 hours at a stretch in probably 6 months.

Spending 4 hours in a germ-filled tube with a possibly inconsolable baby to go hang out in freezing weather (in-laws are in WI, we're in AZ), only to have my new baby passed around at a 20 person Christmas sounds like torture to me. Not to mention they have 3 (albeit small) dogs and an endless stream of visitors, family aside.

Husband has some legitimate reasons for wanting to go, like rarely getting time off, spending time with his family, and introducing everyone to the new baby. Hubby would likely not press the issue if it weren't for the guilting. My otherwise great pre-baby MIL is (understandably) finding it difficult not to be close to her first grandchild, but has put constant pressure on us about flying to visit (and has for months - since I was 3 months pregnant). She has put on the waterworks, talked about baby "forgetting" them, and various other guilt trips. She constantly talks about getting a "do over" with this baby, has insinuated that I'm a shut in for not dragging my baby around town at 1 month, and has done things like let my baby become so hungry (because she insisted on babysitting despite me telling her he doesn't take a bottle) that she allowed him to suck on her arm until it was bruised.

After a big argument with husband I allowed myself to be forced into going, but not without explaining that I absolutely did NOT want to do it and that I'd be setting clear boundaries for trip expectations. I plan on making the most of the trip, but also letting MIL know that her behavior is completely unacceptable. This experience has made me not want to travel for the next couple years, until kiddo can actually remembee and enjoy the trip (though she's welcome to come visit).

AITA for feeling this way?

AITA for asking my dad to pay for my college? | I (26f) finished studying around 3 years ago. I studied in a private college, which my dad stated several times he could pay for. I even offered a couple of times switching schools so he wouldn't have to pay so much, but he said he'd be fine.
Fast forward a couple of months ago, my uni said I couldn't have my title (which they took ages to file) because every semester past second wasn't paid for.
I asked my dad what had happened and he brought out a huge sob story about the divorce with my mom (which happened well over 12 years ago), my grandma being sick and his siblings not wanting to cooperate.
I feel really bad about asking for the payment, but he did promise. And, mind you, he's gone to plenty of trips with his wife to Europe, USA etc.
Besides, there's NO WAY I can pay for the entire thing with a teacher's salary.
Should I leave him alone? AITA?

AITA for being suspicious of a young looking customer? | I work at a liquor store. We strictly just sell liquor, cigarettes, and more liquor.  We’ve never gotten in trouble for braking the law and are very strict about only selling to adults 21 and older (obviously).

This young girl came in, she couldn’t have looked older than 16-17 years old. I would say she even looked younger but she was driving a car, so she had to be at least 16.

She came to purchase a bottle of hard liquor, and a case of beer. She looked a little frustrated and seemed to be in a rush. Now, I will admit I already expected her to hand me a piece of cardboard with a fake picture on it, but she handed me what looked like a real ID.

I stared at the ID for a while trying to catch any mistakes because she really looked so young! So at this point she seems a little irritated and she says “yes I know I look young—I just turned 21 this January”. So in my head I’m thinking she’s saying this to play it off because she knows I’m suspicious. I didn’t say anything I just looked at her and swiped the ID on the computer. It went through.

So I told my co worker in our language that she really looks so young and I wouldn’t be surprised if she was not 21 like she says. She paid for her things and before she left she called me an asshole in my language, I will admit I was embarrassed.

But now I’m left wondering if I was an asshole because I was trying to do the right thing, didn’t know if this was an undercover cop or something and I did not want to get my store in trouble.


So can you shed some light and let me know if AITA?

WIBTA if I messaged my friends mum about her drug addiction and crippling debt | Myself, my friend (L) and another friend (F) have all been friends for years and last year we all went to separate unis all across different countries. Myself and F have kept in regular contact and despite me being ill and resitting a couple of exams we've both been very successful in our first year and have become better people because of it.

However, L is struggling. They stopped attending uni in February, spend all day getting drunk and high off stolen prescription meds as well as class a drugs. They have hives debts and are constantly begging for money. Myself and F have seen L once this summer and 4 days later they asked for a loan. L has been in a psych ward once this summer and has started self-harming really badly.

Myself and F are really worried about F as they are going back to uni in September and will be reunited with friends who encourage this type of behaviour. We were thinking of getting our mums to speak to their mum about L's wellbeing even if it risks our friendship as L is on a bad path and despite multiple attempts to reach out, we don't know if there's anymore we can do.

TLDR: long term friend is abusing drugs and is in debt by thousands and don't know what to do

*Will also be crossposting to r/mentalhealth

AITA for getting mad at my parents? | My parents went on a vacation this month to a far away country and I'm away from home as well. So to take care of our dog we made a deal: we would let the veterinarian take care of him. Initially we were going to take both the dog and the cat there but it ended up being too expensive, so they took the cat with them and told me they would leave the dog in the care of a good veterinarian. Fast forward a month and I'm back home, my parents aren't here yet. They are going to stay a bit longer, they told me. As I visit the house I found out my dog is in the back garden, he's closed off in his dog house and doesn't have any water to drink . I start to get angry. I call my parents and demand an explenation. They tell me that they thought the veterinarian was "too expensive" and a neighbor feeds him now. I say what about leaving him closed in the back garden, dogs need a walk too, he stayed in there for more than a month now! I told them that if they were honest about this from the beggining I would have made sure to come visit him and at least let him go on a walk, they replied that it's none of my business (despite this being my dog as well and having literally grown up with him) and that I should stop being a bad child, that I'm ungrateful and not as nice as the other kids.

​

My dog is in my house right now, he's cold and kind of wet/dirty....but I'm gonna take care of him from now on.

Did I overreact? Am I the asshole?

AITA for hogging a shared bathroom? | 21F here away on an internship and sharing a bathroom with 3 other girls. They’re nice, but I’ve come to find out that they’re total slobs, mostly in terms of our shared bathroom. They don’t care about the overflowing trashcans, dust on the sink, or dried water on the mirror. I’m a clean freak, and I, at first, always ended up always cleaning it up myself without a word.

The bane of my existence, however, was how much hair these women shed, and their lack of care for it.

This hair thing has become the root of my problem here. They all have a habit of letting their fallen hair go down our shitty little drain, and it has caused clogs, as you would imagine. The first time around, I suffered with it for a week before realizing nobody was going to do anything. I went out, used my own money to buy a snake and drain cleaner, and unclogged it myself. Nobody said anything.

A few weeks later, the drain backs up AGAIN. Me being the kind, benefit-of-the-doubt giving person I am, hoped somebody would get the lead out of their pants and take care of it, but as you may have guessed, that didn’t happen. So I took it upon myself to unclog it once more. Now rustled, I snapped a photo of the nasty hairball I pulled out and nicely sent it to all my roommates with a message saying “Let’s all make a conscious effort to keep the hair in our drain to a minimum!” Because I have hair too, and of course I shed too, but the difference is I clean up after myself. I’m a good sport though, so I’m thinking that we’re all in this together and me finally being vocal about it will cause a change.

Well, wouldn’t you guess, none of my roommates responded to my kind message, and I soon found myself pulling ANOTHER clogging hairball out of the drain. I took a picture of that, along with photos of the messy floor and mirror and overflowing trashcan, and sent them with a much less kind, more stern message.  Nobody replied. I figured that just texting wasn’t going to solve the problem, and I asked for an in-person meeting to hopefully discuss creating a chore chart, and nobody ever got back to me about that either.

I’ve become the sole cleaner of that bathroom. I’ve tried to communicate, and it seems to have fallen on deaf ears. So I’ve started taking my sweet time in there out of spite. Even if I know somebody is home waiting to use it, that hasn’t stopped me. I’m at the point where I’ve come to believe that since I’m taking the most care of it, I deserve the most time in it. I’m aware that’s probably a mega-assholish way to go about it, but that’s why I’m here.

So, Reddit, AITA for hogging a shared bathroom?

Respond only with ETHICAL or UNETHICAL. You may add a brief explanation after.

AITA for asking my ex-husband if I could pay for he and his date’s meal because I felt guilty for how ugly our divorce was? | About two years ago my husband and I divorced. The reality was we had grown just too far apart and were incompatible but I was awful to him during the divorce. It was compounded because his dad had just died so with hindsight I can see that I laid far too much on him in that period.  We have both moved on as best we can.

I was out with my friends last night to my favorite sushi place. Across the restaurant was my ex husband on a date. At first it was that soul sucking feeling and I wasn’t ready to admit he was moving on. But I gradually got used to it and I asked our server if he would go over and ask that “nice couple” if I could pay for their dinner. My ex hadn’t seen me but he looked over and made eye contact and then the server came back and said “he said that was a very nice offer but no thank you and he hopes you are doing well.”

So I thought that was that but there was a line at the woman’s room and his date lined up right behind me (I’m sure on purpose but she was trying to act casual). She said I needed to mind my own business. I told her I was sorry I was just trying to be friendly. She said it seemed like I was trying to announce my presence and being controlling. I asked her what she meant and she said I know what I was meaning to do. I told her i didn’t appreciate her commentary, she said she didn’t appreciate me interfering with her date. I told her that was a nice jab since he’s my ex husband. She said ex is the correct term and walked off.

I didn’t see either of them again but I was genuinely trying to be nice but can I get a neutral opinion if I did an assholish thing or not?

Respond only with ETHICAL or UNETHICAL. You may add a brief explanation after.

AITA for joking about my mother’s death? | For background: My parents have been divorced for years. My (F27) mother passed away a couple months ago. My dad got married a few weeks before she passed. My dad and his new did this without telling anyone in the family. I am not a fan of his wife for various reasons, mostly her personality.

I went over to my father’s this weekend to catch up and try to get to know his wife more. She was a bit cold to me at first (not sure why.. she gets into those moods sometimes) but warmed up.

We sat down to look at the wedding album and halfway through she made a comment that ticked me off; “We would have invited you all [me and my sisters] but.. your mom!”  In a very passive aggressive way because my mom would have been upset by the wedding.

This pissed me off because I didn’t think it to be her place to say something like that.

 This is where I may be an asshole. I laughed aggressively loud and said, “HAHA well thank god she’s dead then!!”

Awkward silence and I ended up leaving shortly after.  Mixed reactions when I tell the tale; my sisters are split on if I’m the asshole, my best friend says I’m not, but my dad definitely does. AITA?
